svg.title: Kubernetes
svg.desc: Kubernetes. A container orchestrator: you declare the desired state, and controllers keep pods scheduled, healthy and reachable. Step 1, Where it sits: Catalog runs as 3 pods on 3 nodes; requests reach them via a load balancer, a Gateway and a Service. Step 2, Desired state, controllers: etcd stores the Deployment; controllers make 3 Pods, the scheduler binds them, kubelets start them. Step 3, Self-healing and scaling: node-2 goes silent: its pod leaves the Service and is replaced on node-3. At 90% CPU the HPA sets 5. Step 4, Limits and trade-offs: Requests drive placement, low memory limits mean OOM kills, upgrades are yearly. EKS, AKS, GKE help.

g.text: Catalog runs as 3 pods on 3 nodes; requests reach them via a load balancer, a Gateway and a Service.
etcd stores the Deployment; controllers make 3 Pods, the scheduler binds them, kubelets start them.
node-2 goes silent: its pod leaves the Service and is replaced on node-3. At 90% CPU the HPA sets 5.
Requests drive placement, low memory limits mean OOM kills, upgrades are yearly. EKS, AKS, GKE help.
ClusterIP · sends only to ready pods
v1.37 · ~3 minors a year · ~14 months of patches
the control plane keeps what runs equal to what was declared
The team declares what should run (Deployment catalog: 3 replicas of catalog:1.4.2) and applies it; Kubernetes keeps it running.
Requests go load balancer → Gateway (HTTPRoute /products) → Service catalog → one of the ready pods, on whichever node it runs.
each part: watch the API server → compare desired with actual → act
1 The API server validates the Deployment and 2 stores it in etcd. 3 Controllers create a ReplicaSet, then 3 Pods. 4 The scheduler
binds each to a node with 250m CPU and 256Mi still unrequested. 5 Kubelets start the containers. 6 Ready pods join the Service.
real defaults: 50 s grace · 300 s toleration · HPA checks every 15 s
node-2 stops reporting: after 50 s it is NotReady and its pod leaves the Service; 300 s later the pod is evicted and replaced on node-3.
CPU averages 90% of requests against a 60% target, so the HPA sets ceil(3 × 90 / 60) = 5 replicas; the same load on 5 pods averages 54%.
The scheduler counts requests, not use: set them too high and nodes
fill while idle; set a memory limit too low and the pod is OOMKilled.
Networking (CNI), storage (CSI), RBAC and add-ons need expertise too.
v1.37 (August 2026) is patched until October 2027; a new minor comes
about every 4 months, and the API server moves up one minor at a time.
EKS, AKS and GKE run the control plane; ECS and Cloud Run are simpler.
